short: Context prior from the decoded question (M07) is ahead, gaining in 3 of 3 participants; HMM decoder (M06) is standard; no online accuracy or latency backs the real-time claim.
position: The paper changes two components. Its use-time context (M07), a soft answer prior from the decoded likelihoods of the perceived question, is ahead: no earlier study among 36 dialogue-context matches in 1,280 brain-signal decoding studies (pattern match, inspected as snippets) used such a prior; the deciding priors constrain output with a fixed sentence set or an n-gram model (Moses et al. 2018; Herff et al. 2015), and speller priors come from the user's own previous selections (Speier et al. 2016 review), not a decoded partner utterance; the gain is significant in each of three participants. Its decoder (M06), neural speech-event detection plus phone-HMM Viterbi scoring, is standard, extending the group's perception decoders to produced speech. The authors state that all results are offline simulations and that online runs differed only in hyperparameters, but no online accuracy or latency is measured. Set restriction is an untested confound for the context gain: the restriction and the soft weighting were not separated, and restricting answers by the predicted question gave no improvement.
